scenario: A UX analytics platform only logs user sessions lasting longer than 30 seconds (shorter sessions are classified as bounces and discarded from the engagement database). A product manager uses the average logged session duration to report 'user engagement'.

data.description: Only sessions with duration > 30 seconds are logged. Underlying session durations assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 60 seconds.

question: The engagement database shows a mean session duration of 120 seconds. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean session duration Î¼ across ALL visits (including bounces), and (b) the fraction of all visits that are logged as engaged sessions.
naive_answer: The true mean session duration is approximately 120 seconds since that is the logged average.
naive_trap: Because the truncation threshold (30s) is low relative to the true mean (~109s), only about 9% of sessions are lost. The bias is modest in this case â€” making it a calibration task that tests whether models know to apply the correction even when the magnitude is small.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(30-mu)/60; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+60*norm.pdf(a)/sf-120 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,100,119)
assert abs(mu-108.86)<2.0
assert abs(norm.sf((30-mu)/60)-0.9056)<0.01
